  "text": "His mother did not answer. A pipe knocked inside the ceiling, three patient blows.

“Take your foot back,” his father said.

But the boy had seen the kitchen beyond the other man. On its table stood a blue bowl with a crack through the painted pears. They had thrown that bowl away before he started school. He remembered being allowed to break it the rest of the way, wrapped in newspaper, with a hammer too heavy for him.

Now someone had filled it with oranges.

“That's not today,” he said.

“No,” Anne said.

The other father reached for the wall. His fingers found something the boy couldn't see.

“Don't,” Anne told him.

“She's coming down.”

“Then let her.”

His father got up from the floor. There was dust on one knee, and the boy wanted, absurdly, to brush it off before his mother saw.

“You said it would be empty,” his father said to Anne.

“I said it was empty when I left.”

A stair creaked overhead.

The boy looked down at the label still pinched between his fingers. Its date had changed. He knew the new one: tomorrow. They were meant to drive to his grandmother's after breakfast.

Underneath, a wet stroke of ink appeared.

Almost.

He dropped the key.

Before it touched the floor, his mother said his name from the bottom stair.

Both fathers turned toward her.

She was holding a length of black thread. One end trailed from her hand into the hallway.

“Anne,” she said, “why is his bag coming undone?”"
